tests.name: a runner killed outright reads as interrupted, and its work is ended
tests.reason: Advance the existing host grace timer only after real orphan termination, while retaining real OS signal/process identity and interrupted result assertions. Add guarded exact-owned process group cleanup on every failure.

evidence.independentContract: Workflow design §5.6/§5.8: an outright-killed detached supervisor with no exit record is interrupted, and its recorded process group is terminated safely.
evidence.realRegression: A dead runner leaves its child running, or wait fabricates an ordinary success/exit code instead of an interrupted SIGKILL outcome.
evidence.independentOracle: The fixture starts actual sleep work and kills the supervisor with OS SIGKILL. Literal interrupted=true, code=null, signal=SIGKILL and /proc pid/starttime liveness establish results independently. The documented 5,000 ms host grace is advanced only after real child termination.
evidence.stableSeam: Public SandboxRunner.spawn/wait and OS process identity; native timer mocking controls the existing host Clock scheduling boundary. No result, process signal, filesystem receipt or child liveness is mocked.
evidence.refactorResistance: No private call count, helper arrangement or timer inventory is asserted. The contract is observed through durable child identity, actual process death and public wait result; skipping an unnecessary grace after child death would also pass.
evidence.uniqueProtection: The separate real-time SIGTERM-resistant case owns escalation after the actual 5 s grace. FakeSandbox/engine resume tests cannot prove cleanup of a real orphaned process after an unrecorded runner death. Neither is a substitute for this interrupted-record fixture.
